memories: Run the focused core tests with cargo test -p yoke-core plan:: instead of the whole workspace suite.
Never write to target/release; Codex hooks execute that binary against the real state database.
Store::open applies numbered migrations inside one immediate transaction and checks foreign keys before commit.
Migration 008 rebuilds the plans table to allow the cancelled state; foreign key enforcement is disabled during the rebuild.
The stop guard blocks Stop at most max_blocks times per plan before allowing the agent to finish.
Hook payloads larger than 1 MiB are rejected and recorded as errors.
Use rustfmt --edition 2021 on individual files rather than cargo fmt for the workspace.
redact() masks recognizable secrets like password= and API tokens before anything is written to SQLite.
The console binds to 127.0.0.1 and requires a per-launch token plus CSRF header for mutations.
Memory digest is spawned as a detached process with YOKE_OFF=1 so nested agent hooks stay silent.
Codex Stop fires after every turn, so the digest is debounced to once every 30 minutes per session.
claim_interval in the kv table reserves periodic tasks like the daily update check.
Plan approvals freeze the plan header; editing the header after approval requires re-approval.
yoke trust shows a line-by-line diff and requires typing trust in an interactive terminal.
Agents cannot approve plans: require_human rejects calls from agent tool processes.
Usage ingestion parses transcript JSONL and stores token counts per model in usage_samples.
Unknown model prices must show as unknown instead of zero in cost totals.
The statusline opens the database read-only and never runs migrations.
Release builds for Linux use cargo zigbuild with the x86_64-unknown-linux-musl target.
Integration tests for the CLI live in crates/yoke-cli/tests/core_workflow.rs and roadmap_cli.rs.
The FTS5 index memories_fts is kept in sync with memories by insert, update and delete triggers.
Imported memory archives never carry trust; a human must rerun yoke trust after import.
Retention cleanup prunes decisions and facts older than log.retention_days on SessionStart.
Check runs of unfinished plans are never pruned so evidence survives long builds.
Evidence artifacts are hashed with SHA-256 when a check runs and verified later.
Prefer anyhow::Context for error messages and bail! for early validation failures.
The project uses edition 2021 and rusqlite with the bundled SQLite feature.
Gates run shell commands with a bounded timeout and capped stdout via execute_bounded.
Observe mode records would_deny decisions but never blocks the agent.
Enforce mode denies tool calls when a trusted gate fails.
Config is layered: global ~/.yoke/config.toml then project yoke.toml, and only trusted snapshots apply.
Session start injects pinned memories, trusted knowledge and recent notes within memory.inject_tokens.
yoke share appends a memory to .yoke/knowledge.md but the file still needs human trust.
Symlinked knowledge files are refused to avoid writing outside the project.
Install writes a receipt to ~/.yoke/install-claude.json so uninstall removes only Yoke hooks.
Codex hooks are configured in ~/.codex/hooks.json and require the codex_hooks feature flag.
The update command verifies the release checksum before replacing the executable.
Review runs an independent agent in read-only mode and stores the verdict on the plan.
Review base_ref records the git commit the plan started from so diffs cover only plan work.
Avoid the em dash character in docs; use a plain hyphen.
Markdown docs put one sentence per line to keep diffs readable.
The macOS sed is BSD sed; use perl -i -pe for in-place edits in scripts.
Flaky timing tests should poll for the condition instead of sleeping.
Do not run the full test suite locally; CI runs it.
Console pages are server-rendered HTML; tests assert on the rendered markup in console/tests.rs.
